interface_verification.retained_claim: Existence of a proper birational regular resolution of a normal integral finite-type surface, isomorphic on the regular locus; smoothness over a perfect field.
interface_verification.hypotheses: k has characteristic zero, hence is perfect. C=Spec k[x,y,z]/(xy-z^2) is a finite-type normal integral surface of dimension two. No properness of C over k is assumed or needed.
interface_verification.normality_check: Identify its coordinate ring with k[s^2,t^2,st] in k[s,t] by x=s^2,y=t^2,z=st. It is the invariant ring for (s,t) -> (-s,-t): precisely the even-total-degree monomials. The only defining relation is xy=z^2, as reduction to monomials containing not both x and y gives distinct monomials in s,t. The polynomial ring is finite integral over this subring and is integrally closed. If an element of the subring fraction field is integral over the subring, it is integral over k[s,t], hence lies in k[s,t]; it is invariant, hence lies in the subring. Dimension is two by the finite integral extension. This establishes normality over every permitted characteristic-zero k.
interface_verification.regular_locus_check: D(x) has ring k[x,x^-1,z] and D(y) has ring k[y,y^-1,z], so C is smooth away from its vertex; the vertex has dimension two and embedding dimension three and is singular.

The specific single blowup, smooth exceptional conic and absence of further normalization are the independent chart helper claims, not conclusions inferred from the general theorem.
